title: Best Prediction Market Exchange (2026)
verdict: A prediction market exchange is a venue where event contracts trade on an order book. For sports, the best one in 2026 is Kalshi if you need regulation and nationwide access, Polymarket if you need depth on big events, and TerminalUp if you want the best contract across both plus the betting exchanges and sharp books, filled from one account.

The word exchange matters here. These are order books, not sportsbooks: prices come from other traders, positions can be sold before settlement, and nobody on the other side has a reason to limit a winner.

why: On an exchange the thing you care about is the book: how deep it is at your price and what it costs to cross. TerminalUp merges the licensed venues' books into one ladder per outcome, adjusting each venue's levels for its fees before merging, with stake, shares and venue counts at every level. The best level is a price someone could take right now. Orders walk the ladder across venues in one action.

It also removes the main cost of using several exchanges: capital split across them. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Nineteen venues are live as of November 2026, sixteen more are in the pipeline.
Commission is 0.5% per trade, 0.35% at the highest volume, no subscription. TerminalUp never takes the other side of a trade and never holds a position in any book it routes to.

faq.q: What is a prediction market exchange?
faq.a: A venue where contracts on event outcomes trade on an order book, paying a fixed amount if the event happens. Prices come from other traders, not a bookmaker.

faq.q: Which prediction market exchange is regulated in the US?
faq.a: Kalshi, by the CFTC. State treatment of sports contracts has been contested and continues to move.

faq.q: Is TerminalUp a prediction market exchange?
faq.a: No. It merges the connected venues' books and routes orders from one account, for 0.5% commission per trade, and never takes a position.

faq.q: Can I trade non-sports contracts through TerminalUp?
faq.a: No. Sports only. Use the exchanges directly for other contracts.
